title: The Infinite Software Crisis – Jake Nations, Netflix
talk_summary: Jake Nations argues AI has made code generation 'easy' but not 'simple,' so agents preserve accidental complexity and spiral in long conversational iterations. His fix is a three-phase research → plan → implement workflow that compresses huge codebases into reviewable artifacts (a 2,000-word spec) with human checkpoints before implementation.

takeaways.what_they_do: Feed architecture docs, diagrams, and threads up front; have the agent iteratively map components and dependencies into one research doc; a human validates that analysis before any code is written, then a detailed implementation plan (signatures, types, data flow) is produced and reviewed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the human checkpoint here is critical. This is where you validate the analysis against reality. The highest leverage moment in the entire process.
takeaways.numbers: 5 million tokens compressed to 2,000 words of specification

takeaways.technique: Context compression via curated spec instead of dumping codebase
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of copying large swaths of a 1M-line codebase into context (which got 'lost in its own complexity'), they select design docs, diagrams, key interfaces, and write explicit requirements for how components interact.
takeaways.evidence_quote: 5 million tokens became 2,000 words of specification.

takeaways.technique: Plan-conformance review instead of comprehension review
takeaways.what_they_do: Because the plan is precise ('paint by numbers'), review becomes verifying the implementation conforms to the plan rather than trying to understand whether anything got invented.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can review this quickly because you're just verifying it's conforming to your plan, not trying to understand if anything got invented.

takeaways.technique: Background agent implementation after upfront thinking
takeaways.what_they_do: Once research and plan are done, hand implementation to a background agent and return to review later, since the hard thinking is already captured in artifacts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can use a background agent to do a lot of this work because you've done all the thinking and hard work ahead of time.

takeaways.technique: Seed research with a hand-made reference migration
takeaways.what_they_do: When agents spiraled on an auth refactor, they did one migration manually, then fed that PR in as the seed for research so the agent could see what a clean migration looks like, iterating per-entity for edge cases.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we fed that pull request of the actual manual migration into our research process and had it use that as the seed for any sort of research going forward.

takeaways.technique: Treat every existing pattern as a requirement — explicitly mark debt
takeaways.what_they_do: Warns that agents preserve all patterns equally, including technical debt, so humans must distinguish essential from accidental complexity before starting and tell the agent which patterns to follow.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Technical debt doesn't register as debt. It's just more code.
